history.hpi: Coworkers noticed the patient becoming increasingly confused and diaphoretic over the past 20 minutes during his lunch break; he takes insulin for type 2 diabetes and reportedly skipped lunch today after taking his usual morning insulin dose. He is slurring words and not making sense, though he continues to move all extremities and pushes away hands during examination.
history.lastOralIntake: Coffee only this morning; skipped lunch
history.events: Coworker found him confused and sweating at his desk after his lunch break and called 911

scene.location: Office break room, patient seated in a chair with coworkers gathered nearby
scene.safety: No hazards to crew; patient is restless and pulling away from staff attempting to help
scene.bystanders: Coworker reports patient has been "acting weird" and sweating heavily for the last 20 minutes, confirms he is diabetic
visualCues: Empty insulin pen visible in patient's bag
Patient repeatedly pushing away coworker's hands

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 52-year-old male, confused and profusely diaphoretic, pushing away attempts to assist. Scene glucometer reads BGL 38 mg/dL.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Moves all extremities purposefully but uncooperative, pushes away hands during exam

transitions.condition: Crew confirms hypoglycemia, recognizes the patient is too confused/agitated to safely protect his airway for oral glucose, establishes IV access, and administers dextrose.

phases.name: IV access and dextrose given
phases.description: Crew performs a focused AEIOU-TIPS assessment, confirms BGL 38 mg/dL, and — because the patient is too confused and combative to safely take oral glucose — establishes IV access and administers incremental IV dextrose, securing the line carefully given his agitation.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew recognizes BGL 38 mg/dL with altered mental status too severe for the patient to safely protect his airway for oral glucose, establishes IV access despite the patient's agitation, and administers dextrose per protocol.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses rapid, IV secured to left forearm
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Still uncooperative, resisting arm restraint during line placement
otherFindings: 18ga IV established left forearm on second attempt
Line secured with extra tape given agitation
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Ow— what are you doing to my arm..."

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform focused AEIOU-TIPS assessment; check airway, breathing, circulation, GCS, pupils
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Look for treatable causes of altered mental status (AMS): Airway: Make sure airway remains patent; reposition patient as needed. Breathing: Look for respiratory depression. Circulation: Look for signs of poor perfusion. Glasgow Coma Score and/or AVPU. Pupils.
expectedActions.rationale: Establishes baseline and rules out other causes of AMS before treating.

expectedActions.shortAction: Confirm blood glucose level via glucometer (BGL 38 mg/dL)
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms hypoglycemia as the treatable cause before administering dextrose.

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish IV access; administer Dextrose 25 g (250 mL of D10%) IV in incremental doses, secure site given agitation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Unconscious patient, or patients who are unable to protect their own airway: Dextrose IV – administer in incremental doses until mental status improves or maximum field dosing is reached (if available, D10% is preferred). Maximum field adult dosing: 25 g of 10–50% dextrose IV: 250 mL of 10% dextrose. Dextrose 50% can cause local tissue damage if it extravasates from vein.
expectedActions.rationale: Patient is too confused/combative to safely protect his airway for oral glucose, so IV dextrose is indicated; the extravasation risk is heightened by his agitation, so the line must be well secured.

transitions.condition: Repeat glucose check shows normalization and the patient's mental status clears after incremental dextrose administration; crew prepares for transport with ongoing reassessment.

During placement or dextrose administration, the agitated patient pulls his arm away and the catheter dislodges, causing local swelling and pain at the insertion site before the full dose is delivered.

phases.name: Mental status improved, transport initiated
phases.description: Following incremental IV dextrose, the patient's mental status clears and repeat glucose normalizes. Crew reassesses and prepares for transport.
phases.triggerCondition: After incremental dextrose dosing, the patient's mental status clears and repeat glucose normalizes; crew prepares for transport with ongoing reassessment.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Full strength and cooperative, no longer resisting exam
otherFindings: Embarrassed about earlier combativeness, apologizes to crew
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Whoa — sorry about that, I feel a lot better now. What happened?"

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess vital signs, mental status, and repeat BGL after dextrose administration
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Reassess patient: Reassess vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, neurologic status assessment) and mental status. Repeat check of blood glucose level if previous hypoglycemia and mental status has not returned to normal.
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms treatment effectiveness and identifies any need for further dextrose.

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport to closest appropriate receiving facility given seizure risk history and continued monitoring needs
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If hypoglycemia with continued symptoms, transport to closest appropriate receiving facility.
expectedActions.rationale: Insulin-related hypoglycemia has recurrence risk and warrants evaluation.

phases.name: IV infiltrated during attempt
phases.description: The agitated patient pulls away during dextrose administration and the IV catheter dislodges, causing local swelling and pain at the site before the dose is completed. He remains hypoglycemic and confused.
phases.triggerCondition: During IV placement or dextrose push, the agitated patient pulls his arm away and the catheter dislodges, causing local swelling and pain at the insertion site before the full dextrose dose is delivered.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses rapid; left forearm swollen and tender at IV site
otherFindings: Visible infiltration/swelling at IV site, catheter dislodged
Only partial dextrose dose delivered before infiltration
BGL remains 38 mg/dL, no improvement in mental status

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize IV infiltration, discontinue the line, and reassess for an alternate treatment route
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Dextrose 50% can cause local tissue damage if it extravasates from vein and may cause hyperglycemia.
expectedActions.rationale: Continuing to push dextrose through an infiltrated line risks tissue injury without treating the hypoglycemia.

transitions.condition: With IV access lost and the patient still hypoglycemic and altered, crew administers glucagon IM as the protocol-specified alternative when IV access cannot be established or maintained.

phases.name: Glucagon given after IV failure
phases.description: With the IV line lost, crew administers IM glucagon as the protocol-specified alternative and continues to monitor the patient as it takes effect.
phases.triggerCondition: With IV access lost and the patient still hypoglycemic and altered, crew administers glucagon IM as the protocol-specified alternative when IV access cannot be established or maintained.

otherFindings: Glucagon 1 mg IM administered to deltoid
Mental status gradually clearing over several minutes
Left forearm site dressed, no further attempts on that limb
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I... I think I feel a little better..."

expectedActions.shortAction: Glucagon 1 mg IM to deltoid (adult fixed dose); reassess mental status and repeat BGL
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Glucagon IM/IN – an option for patients for whom IV access cannot be established. Adult dosing: 1 mg IM/IN (or prefilled 3 mg dry powder IN or prefilled IM autoinjector).
expectedActions.rationale: Glucagon is the protocol-specified alternative route when IV access cannot be maintained.

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess vital signs and mental status; transport while monitoring for continued improvement
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Reassess patient: Reassess vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, neurologic status assessment) and mental status.
expectedActions.rationale: Glucagon has a slower onset than IV dextrose and requires ongoing reassessment during transport.
